subject.title: [Bug]: The project won't start on Windows and WSL.

question: Should OpenClaw treat this as a focused Windows/WSL tsdown-wrapper or dependency repair after live repro, or sponsor the broader tsdown-to-tsc rollback requested in the discussion?
rationale: The issue is credible and current code still uses tsdown, but automation cannot safely choose a build-system rollback without Windows/WSL repro logs and maintainer intent on the permanent build toolchain.

options.title: Require focused Windows/WSL repro first
options.body: Run or request a current-main first-build and second-build log on native Windows and WSL before choosing dependency update, wrapper fix, cleanup change, or rollback.

options.title: Promote a broad rollback investigation
options.body: Treat the report as enough to start maintainer-owned work comparing tsdown against tsc across packaging, declarations, and release outputs.

options.title: Hold for reporter logs only
options.body: Keep the issue open but wait for complete reporter logs and environment details before assigning maintainer build-tool time.

recommendation.title: Require focused Windows/WSL repro first
recommendation.body: Run or request a current-main first-build and second-build log on native Windows and WSL before choosing dependency update, wrapper fix, cleanup change, or rollback.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history makes vincentkoc the strongest routing candidate for Windows tsdown wrapper and process handling decisions.
